questions.question: What is the DPO loss formula?
questions.explanation: DPO loss is the negative log-sigmoid of the scaled log-probability ratio between chosen and rejected responses.

questions.question: Why should you use log-space arithmetic instead of computing probabilities directly?
choices: Direct probability computation can overflow/underflow with very small or large values
questions.explanation: Log-probabilities can be very large negative numbers. Computing exp() on them gives 0, and dividing 0/0 gives NaN. Subtracting log-probs is always numerically stable.

questions.question: When the policy model matches the reference model exactly, what is the DPO loss?
questions.explanation: When policy = reference, the ratio is 1, β×1 = β, σ(β) depends on β, but for the standard formulation with β=1, the loss equals log(2). This is the 'no improvement' baseline.
